reference.source: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine / ATS-ERS
clinicalPearls: An inherited cause of early-onset emphysema and chronic liver disease resulting from deficiency of the antiprotease alpha-1 antitrypsin
The emphysema is characteristically basal (lower-zone predominant) and panacinar, in contrast to the upper-zone centrilobular pattern of typical smoking-related disease
Should be suspected in emphysema presenting at a young age, in non-smokers or light smokers, or with a strong family history
The most common severe deficiency genotype is PiZZ, in which misfolded protein is retained in hepatocytes
Liver disease arises from accumulation of abnormally folded protein within hepatocytes and can cause neonatal jaundice, cirrhosis, or hepatocellular carcinoma
Current guidance recommends testing all adults with fixed airflow obstruction/COPD at least once for the deficiency
Smoking dramatically accelerates lung destruction, so cessation and avoidance of exposure are the most important interventions
Intravenous augmentation therapy with purified alpha-1 antitrypsin is available to slow progression of emphysema in appropriately selected deficient patients
reference.pathophysiology: Alpha-1 antitrypsin is a serine protease inhibitor produced mainly by the liver that protects the lung from neutrophil elastase. Deficiency alleles (classically the Z variant) cause the protein to misfold and polymerise within hepatocytes, so little functional protein reaches the circulation and lungs. The resulting protease-antiprotease imbalance allows unopposed elastase activity to destroy alveolar walls, producing panacinar emphysema, a process greatly accelerated by cigarette smoke and other inhaled oxidants. In the liver, retained polymers cause hepatocellular injury and progressive fibrosis.
additionalDifferentials: Other causes of chronic liver disease and cirrhosis
Other genetic or early-onset emphysema syndromes
additionalInvestigations: Serum alpha-1 antitrypsin level as an initial screen
Phenotyping or genotyping to define the deficiency alleles (e.g. PiZZ)
Pulmonary function testing to confirm and grade airflow obstruction with reduced diffusing capacity
High-resolution CT showing basal-predominant emphysema and any bronchiectasis
Liver function tests and imaging, with hepatology assessment for cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance
redFlags: Rapidly progressive breathlessness or frequent exacerbations indicating accelerated lung destruction
Signs of decompensated liver disease such as jaundice, ascites, or variceal bleeding
Features suggesting hepatocellular carcinoma in a patient with established cirrhosis
Continued smoking or ongoing occupational exposure driving rapid decline
reference.prognosis: Prognosis depends heavily on smoking status and genotype; deficient patients who avoid smoke may have near-normal life expectancy, whereas continued exposure leads to accelerated emphysema and respiratory failure, and coexisting liver disease adds risk of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma.
pitfalls: Failing to test for the deficiency in every patient with fixed airflow obstruction as guidelines advise
Assuming a non-smoker cannot have significant emphysema
Neglecting to evaluate and monitor the liver, which is affected independently of the lungs
Omitting family screening and genetic counselling once a deficiency allele is identified
management: Smoking cessation is the single most important intervention to halt accelerated lung destruction; avoid occupational inhaled oxidants
Intravenous augmentation therapy with pooled human alpha-1 antitrypsin is the specific disease-directed treatment for suitable deficient patients with emphysema
Manage airflow obstruction as for COPD with inhaled bronchodilators, inhaled corticosteroids and pulmonary rehabilitation
Vaccinate against influenza, pneumococcus and other respiratory pathogens and treat exacerbations promptly
Monitor lung function and arrange hepatology assessment with surveillance for cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma
Offer family screening and genetic counselling for this inherited disorder
Refer for lung and, where indicated, liver transplantation evaluation in end-stage disease
